palette.notes: Code: 29 colours, mostly phone UI greys; not the art. The tiny canvases use a handful of flat saturated colours (yellow, cyan, navy, green, orange, skin tones) with no ramps.

lighting: None; flat colour blocks on a 4x4 canvas, zoomed huge.
silhouette: At 4x4 pixels the drawings barely read: a yellow face with dark eyes, a skin-tone face with hair; the joke is how much a few pixels can suggest.

motion.timing: Code: median hold 33.3 ms, 13.59 drawings/s, but this is a screen recording of a drawing app; no frame animation.

texture: Giant pixels (pixel_scale 1 on the copy, but each art pixel fills about a quarter of the screen); phone UI and bold outlined captions on top.
camera: Screen recording, vertical; resize dialog first, 'Day 3' title card, then full-screen zoom on the canvas while pixels are placed one at a time.

acting.enters: No characters; the hook is the series premise in the captions over the canvas-size dialog.
acting.acts: Pixels are placed one by one until a face appears.
acting.depth: None; the canvas fills the screen.

techniques: series hook: doubling canvas size every day
captions over the app UI state the premise in 2 s
big title card 'Day 3' for the episode
limited canvas as a challenge constraint
feel: 4x4 canvas + giant flat pixels + daily-doubling series hook = curiosity loop, not craft
for_fred: A pixel-count gag could work: Fred drawn at 4x4, then 8x8, then full size as he swims toward camera. Use it once as a reveal; keep the hook line on screen in the first 2 s.
